column3: And some men came down from Judea and began teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”

And when no small disagreement and debate arose between Paul and Barnabas and them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others from among them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem concerning this question.

So they, having been sent on their way by the assembly, were passing through both Phoenicia and Samaria, describing in detail the conversion of the Gentiles, and they were causing great joy to all the brothers.
When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the assembly and the apostles and elders, and they reported all that God had done with them.
But some from the sect of the Pharisees who had believed stood up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them and command them to keep the law of Moses.”
Then the apostles and elders gathered together to consider this matter.

And after much debate had taken place, Peter stood up and said to them, “Men and brothers, you know that from early days God chose among you that through my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the good news and believe.
And God, who knows hearts, testified to them by giving them the Holy Spirit just as he did to us,
and he made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
Now therefore why are you testing God by putting a yoke on the neck of the disciples that neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus in the same way as they are.”
Then all the multitude became silent, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing what signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
After they became silent, James responded, saying, “Men and brothers, listen to me.
Simeon has described how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for his name.
And with this the words of the prophets agree, just as it is written:
‘After these things I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. I will rebuild its ruins and restore it,
so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles upon whom my name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
known from long ago.’
Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God,
but write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.
For Moses has from ancient generations those proclaiming him in every city, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

Then it seemed good to the apostles and elders, together with the whole assembly, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
They wrote through their hand: “The apostles and the elders, your brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
Since we heard that some from among us, to whom we gave no instructions, went out and troubled you with words, unsettling your souls,
it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men who have handed over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, who themselves will also report the same things by word.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:
to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these things, you will do well. Farewell.”
So when they were dismissed, they went down to Antioch, and gathering the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
And when they read it, they rejoiced at the encouragement.
Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves, encouraged and strengthened the brothers with many words.
And after spending some time, they were sent away with peace from the brothers to those who had sent them.
But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and announcing the good news of the word of the Lord, with many others also.
Now after some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us return and visit the brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are.”
Barnabas wanted to take along John, the one called Mark.
But Paul considered it unworthy to take along this one who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.
And a sharp disagreement occurred, so that they separated from one another. Barnabas took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus.
But Paul chose Silas and went out, having been entrusted by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
And he was passing through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.
